---
name: Vite + TypeScript best practices
description: Best practices for Vite/Vue/TypeScript projects to avoid silent build issues
type: feedback
---

Always set `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` in `tsconfig.app.json` for Vite projects. This causes Vite to prefer `.ts` files over `.js` files during resolution, preventing stale compiled `.js` files from silently shadowing source `.ts` files.

**Why:** We lost hours debugging a search feature that "didn't work" — the root cause was a stale `src/stores/library.js` (probably generated by an earlier `tsc` or `ts-node` run) sitting next to `library.ts`. Vite silently used the old `.js`, so none of our store changes ever made it into the build.

**How to apply:** When starting or inheriting a Vite+TypeScript project:
1. Add `"moduleResolution": "bundler"` to `tsconfig.app.json`
2. Run `find src -name "*.js" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` to check for stale compiled files — any `.js` next to a `.ts` file is suspicious
3. When a build "doesn't work", immediately verify the built output contains your changes: `grep -r 'your_new_function' dist/assets/`
